name: grep-j8
algorithm: app/grep's re variant searched in parallel: walk a generated source tree in mgrep's order, search its files with 8 threads of control, and print every file's path and its count of lines matching an alternation with classes, case-folded, in walk order (README.md).

skip.c: no regex in C's std (app/grep's C cell is lit only)

rust.name: regex
rust.inside: regex-automata 0.4.14 (unsafe code), aho-corasick 1.1.4 and memchr 2.8.0 (unsafe code and SIMD: SSE2 and AVX2 byte and substring searches, Teddy, chosen at run time), regex-syntax 0.8.10 (forbids unsafe code)

rust.name: walkdir
rust.inside: no unsafe code of its own; same-file 1.0.6 and winapi-util 0.1.11 (unsafe Win32 calls through windows-sys 0.61.2 and windows-link 0.2.1) on Windows

models.mk: tasks (M:N on 8 carriers): mgrep -j 8, a feeder task and 8 search tasks over a Chan, a Semaphore of 8 open files, reports printed in file order
models.rust: OS threads: 8 std::thread::scope workers taking file indexes from an AtomicUsize
models.go: goroutines (GOMAXPROCS 8): 8 workers taking file indexes from a channel
models.cs: OS threads: 8 System.Threading.Thread workers taking file indexes via Interlocked.Increment

notes: The Mk side is the mgrep dogfood, unchanged (package Dogfoods/mgrep), at -j 8 with MK_CARRIERS=8 (the concurrency row's thread count, B19). Its single-threaded form is app/grep.
The input is app/grep's tree (tools/bench gen kind tree, seed 5, bytes 100,000,000; the same directory). The size is provisional: verify -publish-size in the coordinator's window fixes it.
The checksum is the SHA-256 of the output with the tree's path written back as $DATA; it equals app/grep's re variant's, since the output does not depend on the number of threads.
Rust: regex 1.12.3 and walkdir 2.5.0 from the same cargo vendor tree in Mk-evidence as app/grep (crates), by directory source replacement (D-835).
